title: Hedged Dedicated Pools & Adaptive Autoscale — Q2 Planning and Measurement Framework
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Define and validate a quarterly roadmap slice for hedged dedicated GPU pools and an adaptive autoscale control plane that reduces cost without compromising customer SLOs. Scope includes: (1) a hedging policy to reserve short-duration buffer capacity for predictable traffic spikes, (2) an adaptive autoscaler that combines predictive signals (forecasted demand) with reactive rules (latency and queuing signals), and (3) a measurement plan to quantify cost savings, SLO adherence, and failover behavior.

Why now: Dedicated commitments and customer SLAs make rigid reserved pools costly and brittle. We need a pragmatic approach that buys predictable capacity for critical customers while allowing opportunistic reuse for lower tiers. This ticket captures product trade-offs, success metrics, rollout gating, and the cross-functional work required to ship a Q2 pilot.

Constraints: must work with existing Dedicated control plane, respect isolation/tenant labels for billing, support resume/freeze workflows for reserved pools, and integrate with Console dashboards. Security review may be required for billing telemetry changes.

Deliverables: PRD describing hedging policy and autoscaler modes; measurement dashboard (cost per token, 95th/99th latency by route and model, failover incidents); pilot plan (two enterprise customers + internal synthetic traffic); rollout guardrails and rollback plan.
acceptance_criteria: PRD accepted by Eng and SRE with trade-off matrix and one annotated runbook
Autoscaler prototype deployed in a staging Dedicated pool controlling at least 1 GPU cluster
Hedging policy implemented: configurable reservoir window and priority-based allocation
Measurement dashboard ingests billing and latency signals; baseline vs pilot comparison visible
Pilot reduces average per-token cost for targeted workloads by >= 12% without increasing P95 latency > 10%
Rollout playbook with canary thresholds, abort conditions, and postmortem template completed
comments: 2025-01-20 — Kickoff with Eng (Marco), SRE (Ruth), and Finance (Sam): aligned on KPI targets and pilot customers. Action: Marco to scope autoscaler APIs and Ruth to sketch required telemetry events.
2025-01-27 — Decision: start with a conservative hedging window (1–3 hours) and two priority tiers; use reservation labels rather than hard-tenancy to enable safe reuse.
2025-02-03 — Architecture review feedback from Eng: prefer event-driven refill over polling to reduce control-plane overhead. Eng team to prototype refill lambda and expose health metrics.

2025-02-07 — PM review: refine success metric to emphasize customer-visible SLOs first (P95 latency, queue length) and secondarily cost per token. Finance asked for cost sensitivity scenarios at -20%/+20% traffic.
2025-02-12 — Design check-in: Console team requests an explicit UI mode to opt-in to hedged pools and visibility into what percentage of capacity is hedged vs shared.
2025-02-14 — Status: Prototype autoscaler control loop merged to staging (ENG-4871). Next: run 72h synthetic stress test and capture dashboard metrics.
notes: Trade-offs considered: larger hedging windows reduce cold-starts but increase capital commitment; we will expose window size per customer tier.
Fallback policy: autoscaler must support immediate fallback to shared-hosted models if hedged pool health degrades; this is a soft-degradation path with elevated cost alerts.
Open question: billing granularity for hedged capacity (per-minute vs per-hour). Finance prefers per-minute for fairness; implementation depends on cloud reservation SKU limits.
Risk log: (1) telemetry gaps could mask queuing (mitigation: add queue_length event), (2) billing disputes (mitigation: detailed per-request attribution logs).
